Reconcile forecast draws over a hierarchy

Source: R/hierarchy.R
mt_reconcile.Rd

Makes forecasts of nested or crossed strata add up, draw by draw. For each age, year and draw, the base forecasts y of all strata in the hierarchy (bottom series and aggregates) are projected onto the coherent subspace, y - W U (U' W U)^-1 U' y, where U' y = 0 are the aggregation constraints (each aggregate equals the sum of its bottom series). With additive = "deaths" in the hierarchy, the projection works on expected deaths (rates times exposures; exposures of aggregates are the sums of their bottom series), and reconciled rates are reconciled deaths divided by exposures. Methods choose W:

Usage

mt_reconcile(
  draws,
  hierarchy = NULL,
  method = c("wls", "mint", "structural", "ols", "bottom_up", "proportional"),
  shrink = "auto",
  exposure = NULL,
  dependence = c("empirical", "none"),
  seed = NULL,
  fixed = NULL,
  var = NULL,
  total = NULL,
  parts = NULL
)

Arguments

draws

An mt_draws object with the strata of the hierarchy.

hierarchy

An mt_hierarchy() (or, for one variable, var and total).

method

"wls" (default), "mint", "structural", "ols", "bottom_up" or "proportional" (with fixed). The vignette "Coherent forecasts: totals and their parts" compares them.

shrink

Shrinkage intensity for "mint" (number between 0 and 1), or "auto".

exposure

Exposures [age, period, stratum] or [age, stratum] for the forecast years (default: last training year). Only bottom strata are used, and they are enough; aggregates are summed.

dependence

"empirical" or "none" (keep the draws as they are).

seed

Random seed for the reordering.

fixed

Strata whose forecasts are kept unchanged (labels, or "total" for the grand total of the hierarchy), for example a trusted all-cause forecast that the causes must add up to. The projection gives these nodes zero variance, so the other strata absorb the whole gap; $reconciliation$max_relative_change_fixed reports how closely they were kept; they move, with a warning, when their own forecasts do not add up (a node fixed together with all its parts) or when every bottom stratum below them would have to be negative. Needs a projection method or "proportional".

var, total, parts

One-variable form: stratum variable and its total level (parts is ignored: all other levels are parts).

Value

The reconciled mt_draws, with diagnostics in $reconciliation (method, largest relative gap before reconciliation, share of bottom values held at zero, mean shrinkage intensity).

Details

  • "mint": covariance of the base draws across strata, shrunk towards its diagonal (Schaefer-Strimmer intensity by default). This follows the minimum-trace reconciliation of Wickramasuriya et al. (2019), with the covariance of the forecast draws in place of in-sample residuals;

  • "wls": diagonal with the variance of each stratum's draws;

  • "structural": diagonal with the number of bottom series in each node;

  • "ols": identity;

  • "bottom_up": aggregates are the sums of the bottom forecasts.

Projections can make bottom values negative where the base forecasts disagree strongly. Such values are held at zero and the remaining bottom strata of the draw are projected again, until none is negative (a simple form of the non-negative reconciliation of Wickramasuriya et al. 2020); the aggregates are recomputed from the bottom series, so the result is coherent and non-negative, and fixed nodes are kept. A warning reports when more than 5% of the draws needed this, because the distributions of the affected strata (often small causes) are then truncated at zero.

"proportional" keeps the fixed nodes and scales the bottom strata below each of them in proportion to their own forecasts, draw by draw (top-down allocation with forecast proportions, Athanasopoulos, Ahmed and Hyndman 2009). It never sets a part to zero and keeps the shape of the parts' distributions; it is the usual choice when causes of death must add up to a trusted all-cause forecast. Fixed nodes must not share parts.

Draws of strata forecast by separate models are independent, so their sums would be too narrow. With dependence = "empirical" (default), the paths of each stratum are first reordered so that their ranks follow the co-movement of the strata in the training data (an empirical copula, the "Schaake shuffle" of Clark et al. 2004): every draw is matched to a training year, and the stratum whose average year-to-year change of log rates was relatively large in that year receives a relatively high path. The marginal distribution of each stratum is unchanged.

The one-variable interface with var and total is still accepted. It reconciles deaths when the exposures of the parts add up to that of the total (sexes, regions) and rates when each part has the exposure of the total (causes of death) or there are no exposures; give a hierarchy with additive to choose.

References

Wickramasuriya SL, Athanasopoulos G, Hyndman RJ (2019). Optimal forecast reconciliation for hierarchical and grouped time series through trace minimization. Journal of the American Statistical Association 114(526): 804-819. doi:10.1080/01621459.2018.1448825

Athanasopoulos G, Ahmed RA, Hyndman RJ (2009). Hierarchical forecasts for Australian domestic tourism. International Journal of Forecasting 25: 146-166.

Wickramasuriya SL, Turlach BA, Hyndman RJ (2020). Optimal non-negative forecast reconciliation. Statistics and Computing 30: 1167-1182. doi:10.1007/s11222-020-09930-0

Clark M, Gangopadhyay S, Hay L, Rajagopalan B, Wilby R (2004). The Schaake shuffle: a method for reconstructing space-time variability in forecasted precipitation and temperature fields. Journal of Hydrometeorology 5(1): 243-262.

Schaefer J, Strimmer K (2005). A shrinkage approach to large-scale covariance matrix estimation and implications for functional genomics. Statistical Applications in Genetics and Molecular Biology 4(1): Article 32. doi:10.2202/1544-6115.1175

Examples

x <- mt_example_regions(years = 2005:2019, regions = 3)
h <- mt_hierarchy(sex = "both", region = "all", quintile = "all")
xa <- mt_aggregate_strata(x, h)
fc <- mt_forecast(mt_fit(lee_carter(), xa), h = 3, n_draws = 50, seed = 1)
rc <- mt_reconcile(fc, h, method = "wls")
rc$reconciliation
#> $method
#> [1] "wls"
#> 
#> $max_relative_gap_before
#> [1] 0.3081628
#> 
#> $share_set_to_zero
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $mean_shrinkage
#> [1] NA
#> 
#> $share_draws_with_zeros
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $max_relative_change_fixed
#> [1] NA
#>
